title: 2000 AMC 10 Problem 17
statement: Boris has an incredible coin changing machine. When he puts in a quarter, it returns five nickels; when he puts in a nickel, it returns five pennies; and when he puts in a penny, it returns five quarters. Boris starts with just one penny. Which of the following amounts could Boris have after using the machine repeatedly?

solutions.text:
Trading a quarter for five nickels or a nickel for five pennies does not change the total value. Only trading a penny for five quarters changes it, adding \(5 \cdot 25 - 1 = 124\) cents.

Starting from \(1\) cent, Boris always has \(1 + 124n\) cents for some nonnegative integer \(n.\)

Only \(\$7.45\) has this form, since \(745 = 1 + 124 \cdot 6.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: A quarter for five nickels and a nickel for five pennies each leave the total value unchanged
Only the penny-for-five-quarters trade changes the total, always adding \(\$1.24\)
